A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA and confidence-estimation experiments on NQ, HotpotQA, and MMLU, including C3 evaluations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical comparisons of internal-state confidence with three alternative confidence-estimation methods in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The internal-state extraction, four-layer MLP, and C3 question-reformulation and calibration procedures remain unchanged. Equation 6 and Figure 4 are corrected to match the binary classification and calibration rules already described in v1; they do not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, HotpotQA, and MMLU with the same task coverage. The added baseline comparison reuses NQ and HotpotQA without introducing a new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix A.6 and Figure 8 add evaluated probabilistic confidence (Prob), verbalized confidence (Verb), and semantic-consistency confidence (Consis) baselines against Align-A across four models on NQ and HotpotQA. V1 discusses alternative confidence methods but lacks this empirical comparison, so the comparator coverage expands substantially.

E3.justification: The added comparison introduces confidence-threshold selection using training/development data, with 10,000 training examples per dataset. Consis uses ten sampled responses at temperature 0.8 and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct for semantic judging. Protocols for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a limited computational-cost analysis, counting five inference calls for C3's reformulation/calibration stages versus 21 for the implemented semantic-consistency comparison. This is analytical call accounting, not a measured latency experiment. Existing sensitivity, candidate-answer, reformatted-question, and training-size analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify training the confidence estimator with seeds 0, 42, and 100 and reporting average performance. V2 adds no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Consis's ten sampled answers are part of its estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 8 adds substantial comparative result evidence, reporting Align-A above all three added baselines across the evaluated model/dataset combinations. For Llama2-7B on NQ, Verb, Consis, and Prob score 62.7, 71.7, and 74.4, versus Align-A's 77.9. The Align-A values are rounded redisplays of Table 6; the existing Tables 1–11 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 6 changes from taking the maximum class probability to taking argmax over the binary labels. This corrects a mathematical definition that previously returned a probability instead of the stated class label. No theorem, proof, or other substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about pre-generation perception, stable pre/post-generation gaps, and C3's benefits. The headline UPR improvements remain 5.6% on NQ and 4.9% on HotpotQA. C3's expanded name changes without redefining its contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an empirical rationale for choosing internal-state confidence as the baseline, while A.7 argues that confidence-consistency calibration requires fewer inference calls than semantic-consistency estimation. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning binary confidence, factual knowledge, and model scale are retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents the added baselines' sampling, semantic judge, and threshold-selection settings, and explains C3's inference-call composition. The first-page repository link changes from the ShiyuNee namespace to Trustworthy-Information-Access. Existing MLP hyperparameters and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Manakul et al. (2023), SelfCheckGPT, as a reference for semantic-consistency confidence and expands the comparison with alternative confidence families in Appendix A.6. The main related-work organization and overall research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 renames C3 to Confidence Consistency-based Calibration, revises the analysis-dimensions paragraph, updates affiliations and corresponding-author information, and adds acknowledgements and Appendices A.6–A.7. The existing narrative and section structure are largely preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds the baseline bar chart in Figure 8 and revises Figure 4's decision labels so the true calibration condition leads to No, matching Equation 7. There are small diagram styling changes and text/table reflow, while existing result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful direct evidence for the internal-state baseline choice through Appendix A.6/Figure 8 and fixes the incorrect label formula in Equation 6 and reversed workflow branches in Figure 4. These strengthen support and clarity without changing the original findings. The added efficiency discussion is informative but limited to inference-call accounting rather than measured end-to-end cost.
